name: Cat's Claw
summary: Cat's Claw (Uncaria tomentosa) carries a Grade C rating — limited evidence. Strongest recorded design is a narrative review, drawn from 3 recorded studies, none of which measured an outcome in people. Recorded activity centres on inflammatory signaling modulation, immune signaling modulation and NF-kB modulation, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include pregnancy/breastfeeding without clinician supervision and known allergy to the plant/family.
description: Cat's Claw botanical profile with evidence, safety, and practical fit.
safetyNotes: IMMUNE AND PREGNANCY CAUTION: Cat's claw (Uncaria tomentosa) might stimulate immune activity and may interact with immunosuppressant medicines. Transplant recipients should not self-medicate because of a theoretical risk of interfering with anti-rejection treatment; actual transplant rejection caused by cat's claw is NOT established. Avoid use during pregnancy; breastfeeding safety is uncertain. Possible bleeding and blood-pressure medication interactions are primarily theoretical or based on limited evidence. Human efficacy evidence remains inconclusive (NCCIH).
contraindications: Transplant recipients or people taking immunosuppressants: avoid unsupervised use
Autoimmune disease: seek clinical advice before use
interactions: use clinician review for high-dose extracts or chronic use.
Potential interference with immunosuppressants (theoretical; clinical outcome not established)
Possible interactions with anticoagulants/antiplatelets and antihypertensive medicines; evidence is limited
